The chapter builds the decay chain $A \to B \to \emptyset$ of [Get started](cppDE.html) with
several integrators, compiles the variants together and reads the result of `solveODE()`.

```{r library}
library(cppDE)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Model definition

[`cppODE()`](../reference/cppODE.html) takes the right-hand sides as a named character vector,
the names being the states. Every other symbol is a parameter. `modelname` names the source file
and the exported C symbols, `outdir` the directory of the source (default `tempdir()`). With
`compile = FALSE` the source is written and nothing is compiled.

```{r define}
eqns  <- c(A = "-k1*A", B = "k1*A - k2*B")
parms <- c(A = 1, B = 0, k1 = 0.5, k2 = 0.2)
times <- seq(0, 10, by = 0.1)

chain <- cppODE(eqns, modelname = "g1_chain", outdir = tempdir(), compile = FALSE)
attr(chain, "variables")
attr(chain, "parameters")
basename(attr(chain, "srcfile"))
```

`method` selects the integrator, `stepTrace = TRUE` records every step attempt (see
[Diagnostics](#diagnostics)).

```{r define-methods}
adams <- cppODE(eqns, method = "adams", modelname = "g1_adams", compile = FALSE)
rb4   <- cppODE(eqns, method = "rb4",   modelname = "g1_rb4",   compile = FALSE)
tsit5 <- cppODE(eqns, method = "tsit5", modelname = "g1_tsit5", compile = FALSE)
traced <- cppODE(eqns, deriv = FALSE, stepTrace = TRUE, modelname = "g1_traced",
                 compile = FALSE)
```

Further arguments of `cppODE()`: `events`, `forcings` and `rootfunc` ([chapter 2](guide-events.html),
[chapter 5](guide-steady-states.html)); `deriv`, `deriv2` and `fixed` ([chapter 3](guide-sensitivities.html));
`derivMode` ([chapter 4](guide-reverse.html)); `profile = TRUE` compiles timers that print a
summary per category to the standard error stream after each solve; `verbose = TRUE` reports the
steps of code generation.

## Expression language

Right-hand sides, event values, roots and the equations of `cppFUN()` share one
[expression language](../reference/expressions.html): R syntax with `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `^`,
the common elementary functions, comparisons and logical operators that give 1 or 0, and the
switches `piecewise()`, `ifelse()`, `Heaviside()` and `sign()`. `time` is the independent variable
and `pi` the number.

## Joint compilation

[`compile()`](../reference/compile.html) builds the generated sources. With `output` they link into
one shared object in the directory of the first source; `cores` runs the compiler jobs in parallel,
`args` appends compiler flags, `verbose = TRUE` shows the commands.

```{r compile}
compile(chain, adams, rb4, tsit5, traced, output = "guide1", cores = 2)
```

The flags of a model, such as the step trace, apply to the source of that model only.

The environment variables `CPPDE_EXTRA_CXXFLAGS` and `CPPDE_EXTRA_LIBS` add flags to every
compilation of the session. A model recompiled into a shared object of another name needs
[`clearNativeSymbols()`](../reference/clearNativeSymbols.html); `compile()` calls it itself.

## Solution and output

[`solveODE()`](../reference/solveODE.html) takes the model, the output times and a named vector of
initial values and parameters.

```{r solve}
out <- solveODE(chain, times, parms)
str(out[c("time", "variable", "tangent")])
out$variable[101, ]
```

| element | content |
|:--|:--|
| `time` | output times, `n_t` |
| `variable` | states, `[n_t, n_x]` |
| `tangent` | first-order sensitivities, `[n_t, n_x, n_s]` ([chapter 3](guide-sensitivities.html)) |
| `hessian` | second-order sensitivities, `[n_t, n_x, n_s, n_s]` ([chapter 3](guide-sensitivities.html)) |
| `cotangent`, `curvature`, `correction`, `store`, `adjoint` | reverse mode ([chapter 4](guide-reverse.html)) |
| `diagnostics` | solver statistics |
| `trace` | step trace, with `stepTrace = TRUE` |

The initial values hold at time 0. With `includeTimeZero = TRUE` (default of `cppODE()`) the
time 0 is added to the output grid, so a grid that starts later still starts from them.

```{r time-zero}
solveODE(chain, c(5, 10), parms)$time
```

## Tolerances and step control

`abstol` and `reltol` (default `1e-6`) bound the local error of every step. `hini` sets the first
step (default `0`, estimated), `maxsteps` the total number of steps, `maxattempts` the number of
attempts without progress. `onFailure` decides what an unsuccessful solve returns: `"stop"`
(default) is an error, `"warn"` and `"silent"` return the rows up to the time reached.

```{r failure}
part <- solveODE(chain, times, parms, maxsteps = 20, onFailure = "warn")
part$diagnostics[c("return_code", "t_reached")]
```

## Diagnostics {#diagnostics}

[`diagnostics()`](../reference/diagnostics.html) prints the statistics of a solve; the list itself
is `$diagnostics`.

```{r diagnostics}
diagnostics(out)
```

A model compiled with `stepTrace = TRUE` returns one row per step attempt as `$trace`, with step
size `h`, order `q` and error test value `dsm`; `traceFile` writes the same to a CSV file.

```{r trace, fig.height = 3}
tr <- solveODE(traced, times, parms)$trace
head(tr[, c("t", "h", "q", "dsm", "mode")], 4)

ggplot(tr, aes(t, h, color = factor(q))) +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "time", y = "step size", color = "order")
```

The first step of `"bdf"` and `"adams"` follows CVODES: a state that starts at zero with a non-zero
rate bounds it by about `abstol` over that rate, here $B$. From there the step grows by up to a
factor of $10^4$, so the small start costs two or three steps
([the first step](methods-stepping.html#the-first-step)).

## Integration methods

The chain is solved with every method, once as given and once stiff, with `k1 = 1000`.

```{r methods}
models <- list(bdf = chain, adams = adams, rb4 = rb4, tsit5 = tsit5)
stiff  <- replace(parms, "k1", 1000)
count  <- function(p) sapply(models, function(m)
  unlist(solveODE(m, times, p)$diagnostics[c("accepted", "fevals", "setups")]))
count(parms)
count(stiff)
```

Further arguments of `solveODE()` and `cppODE()` adjust the integrator:

- `maxOrder` bounds the order of `"bdf"` (1 to 5) and `"adams"` (1 to 12).
- `stald = TRUE` lowers the BDF order when the step leaves the stability region of the order.
- `useNDF = FALSE` (in `cppODE()`) takes the classical BDF coefficients instead of the NDF ones.
- `sparse` (in `cppODE()`) chooses sparse LU by KLU (`TRUE`), dense LU (`FALSE`) or decides from
  the sparsity of the Jacobian (`NULL`, default). KLU is optional at install time,
  [Installation](installation.html).
- `useDenseOutput = FALSE` (in `cppODE()`) makes `"rb4"` and `"tsit5"` land on every output time
  instead of interpolating.

```{r order}
sapply(1:5, function(q) solveODE(chain, times, parms, maxOrder = q)$diagnostics$accepted)
```

### Choice of integrator

| situation | choice | details |
|:--|:--|:--|
| stiff or unknown | `"bdf"` (default) | [Stepping: BDF](methods-stepping.html#backward-differentiation-formula-bdf) |
| large, sparse Jacobian | `"bdf"` with `sparse = TRUE` | [Installation](installation.html) |
| stiff, frequent events or switches, moderate size | `"rb4"`, one-step, restarts at full order | [Stepping: Rosenbrock](methods-stepping.html#rosenbrock-rb4), [Events](methods-events.html#restart-after-an-event) |
| non-stiff | `"tsit5"` | [Stepping: Tsitouras](methods-stepping.html#tsitouras-tsit5) |
| non-stiff, smooth, long horizon | `"adams"` | [Stepping: Adams-Moulton](methods-stepping.html#adams-moulton-adams) |
| BDF unstable at high order on oscillating modes | `stald = TRUE` or `maxOrder` | [Step-size control](methods-stepping.html#adaptive-step-size-control) |
| the CVODES implementation of SUNDIALS | `cvode()` | [chapter 8](guide-cvode.html), [cvode()](methods-cvode.html) |
